propositions: os.makedirs(ticket_dir) ran outside the write lock before the first event file was written, creating a window where an interruption (host sleep, kill, timeout) leaves an empty ticket directory orphaned in the worktree, reported by fsck as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH.

Directory and first event are now staged atomically in a dot-prefixed staging path (.tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex>) then published with a single os.rename() under the existing write lock, ensuring no fsck-visible path is left if creation is interrupted.

The leading-dot naming convention leverages existing fsck exclusion rules (fsck._ticket_dirs, fsck.foreign_store_path_list already skip dot-prefixed top-level entries), making temp paths invisible to both checks without scanner changes.

batch_stage_and_commit, inbound_translate._write_event_file, and dispatch_one BRIDGE_ALERT emission all shared the same mkdir-then-file vulnerability and were converted to use the same atomic staging+promote pattern.

Bounded, best-effort sweep of stale .tmp-newticket-* dirs owned by dead processes (using write-lock v2 stamp: host + pid-namespace + start-time) runs at writer start to clean up orphaned staging areas, respecting bug 043f boundary (never touches ticket directories or store data).
